meta.title: Heaven: The End of the Story
meta.verseText: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Look! God's dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.' He who was seated on the throne said, 'I am making everything new!'
meta.theme: God will make everything right in the end!

questions.text: Who wrote the book of Revelation?
questions.hint: He was one of Jesus' closest friends.
questions.explanation: John, one of Jesus' closest friends, wrote the book of Revelation.

questions.text: Where was John when he wrote Revelation?
questions.explanation: John was exiled on a remote island called Patmos for telling people about Jesus.

questions.text: Why was John on the island of Patmos?
options: He was exiled for telling people about Jesus
questions.explanation: John was exiled to Patmos as punishment for telling people about Jesus.

questions.text: What is our Bottom Line this week?
options: God will make everything right in the end!
questions.hint: It's about how the story ends.
questions.explanation: Our Bottom Line is: 'God will make everything right in the end!'

questions.text: According to Revelation 21, what will God wipe from our eyes?
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 says God will wipe every tear from their eyes.

questions.text: True or False: In the new heaven and new earth, there will be no more death or pain.
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 promises no more death, mourning, crying, or pain.

questions.text: Revelation says God will dwell with His ______.
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 says God's dwelling place is among the people.

questions.text: What did God on the throne say He is making?
questions.explanation: God said, 'I am making everything new!' in Revelation 21:5.

questions.text: True or False: The Bible says brokenness came into the world because of sin.
questions.explanation: When sin entered the world, brokenness came with it, affecting everything and everyone.

questions.text: Why does life sometimes feel hard, even when we believe in God?
options: We live in a broken world
questions.explanation: Living in a broken world means we still face hard things, but it doesn't mean something is wrong with our faith.

questions.text: What does it mean when we ask questions about why bad things happen?
options: We're living in a broken world
questions.explanation: Asking hard questions doesn't mean something is wrong with your faith; it means you're living in a broken world.

questions.text: What are the 'trail markers' in our lesson?
options: Truths God gives us about the end of our story
questions.explanation: The trail markers represent truths God gives us about the end of our story in Revelation.

questions.text: Knowing where the trail ends changes how we walk through the ______.
questions.explanation: Knowing where the trail ends changes how we walk through the middle of our journey.

questions.text: True or False: Following God means life will suddenly be easy.
questions.explanation: Following God doesn't mean life is suddenly easy, but hard things aren't the end of the trail.

questions.text: What is God doing with the story of the world right now?
options: He's still writing it and moving toward restoration
questions.explanation: God isn't finished yet; He is moving the story toward restoration and healing.

questions.text: When you feel disappointed, what should you remember?
options: God is still writing the story
questions.explanation: When you face disappointment, remember that God is still writing the story and one day He will wipe away every tear.

questions.text: Hard things in life aren't the ______ of the trail.
questions.explanation: Today's story reminds us that hard things aren't the end of the trail.

questions.text: Which book of the Bible tells us about the end of the story?
questions.hint: It's the last book of the Bible.
questions.explanation: Revelation is the last book of the Bible and tells us about how God will make all things new.

questions.text: What is one thing the Bible says will NOT be in heaven?
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:4 says there will be no more death, mourning, crying, or pain.

questions.text: True or False: God's plan is to fix the broken world and make everything right.
options: Only after we fix it ourselves
questions.explanation: The exciting part is God has a plan to fix everything and make it right in the end.

questions.text: What should we do when answers to our questions take time?
options: Keep going and don't give up
questions.explanation: We don't have to give up when things feel heavy or lose hope when answers take time.

questions.text: Which of these is a good way to apply today's lesson at school?
options: Remember God is still writing your story
questions.explanation: In the middle of school and stress, remember that God isn't finished yet and is moving the story toward restoration.

questions.text: When a friend goes through something hard, what is a Christ-like response?
options: Remind them God will make everything right in the end
Tell them to stop being sad
questions.explanation: We can encourage friends by sharing the hope that God is still writing the story and will make everything right.

questions.text: How does knowing about heaven help us today?
options: It makes us forget about today
It gives us hope to keep going
It makes us want to leave now
questions.explanation: Knowing the ending of the story helps us keep going right now.

questions.text: True or False: Asking hard questions about God means your faith is broken.
questions.explanation: Those questions don't mean something is wrong with your faith; they mean you're living in a broken world.

questions.text: What did Jesus' friend John see visions of on Patmos?
options: The end of the story and the new heaven
questions.explanation: While exiled on Patmos, John saw visions of the end of the story, including the new heaven and new earth.

questions.text: In the new heaven, God Himself will be with them and be their ______.
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 says God Himself will be with them and be their God.

questions.text: What did the voice from the throne announce about God's dwelling place?
options: It is now among the people
questions.explanation: The voice said, 'God's dwelling place is now among the people.'

questions.text: What does the word 'restoration' mean in our lesson?
options: Making things new and right again
questions.explanation: Restoration means God is making everything new and right again, healing what is broken.

questions.text: True or False: We have to fix the world ourselves before God will help.
questions.explanation: God is the one who has the plan to fix the world; we don't have to do it on our own.

questions.text: Our Conversation Starter is: What do you think ______ will be like?
questions.explanation: Our Conversation Starter is: 'What do you think Heaven will be like?'

questions.text: Who helps us continue to make wise choices, even when life is hard?
questions.explanation: With the help of the Holy Spirit, we can continue to make wise choices.

questions.text: What attitude should we have when we don't understand why hard things happen?
questions.explanation: We can trust God and keep going because He is still writing the story and will make everything right.

story.summary: The apostle John, one of Jesus' closest friends, was exiled to a remote island called Patmos because he kept telling people about Jesus. While he was there, God gave him amazing visions about the end of the story. John wrote what he saw in the book of Revelation. He saw a new heaven and a new earth, and a loud voice from the throne announced that God's dwelling place would now be among His people. God would wipe away every tear, and there would be no more death, mourning, crying, or pain. God Himself said, 'I am making everything new!' This is the ending of God's story for us: He will make everything right in the end. Even though we live in a broken world where hard things happen, knowing how the story ends gives us hope to keep going right now.

scenes.title: John on Patmos
scenes.description: John, Jesus' close friend, is exiled to a remote island called Patmos because he keeps telling people about Jesus. He is alone, but God is about to give him an incredible vision of the end of the story.

scenes.title: A Broken World
scenes.description: John knows what we know — the world is a mix of good things and hard things. Brokenness came in when sin entered, and that's why we sometimes feel sad or confused. But asking hard questions doesn't mean our faith is broken.

scenes.title: The Voice from the Throne
scenes.description: In John's vision, a loud voice from the throne announces: God's dwelling place is now among His people! He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.

scenes.title: Making Everything New
scenes.description: God on the throne declares, 'I am making everything new!' This is the trail marker that tells us how the story ends — God will restore and heal everything. Heaven is coming.

scenes.title: Walking the Middle of the Trail
scenes.description: Knowing where the trail ends changes how we walk the middle. When school is stressful or life feels heavy, we remember: God is still writing the story. Hard things aren't the end of the trail.
